title: GraphNous Scan Result
description: Result produced by a GraphNous scanner for a single scan target. Qualified names identify declarations across the result, so calls, field accesses and type references can be linked to them. They follow the conventions of each language: Java uses package and class names, and methods add their parameter types, e.g. "com.example.Orders.find(java.lang.String)". TypeScript and JavaScript use the file path relative to the target without its extension, a colon, then the dotted name, e.g. "src/orders:Orders.find". What calling a value of a callable type calls, its call signature or the function type of a type alias, is named "call" after the type, e.g. "src/client:Client.call" for client(url) with client: Client. Declarations of the TypeScript built-in library, the JavaScript built-ins and the DOM, have their global name without a path, e.g. "Array.isArray", "Promise.race" or "console.log", with constructors as "TypeError.constructor". Declarations of npm packages are named after the module they are imported from, a colon, then the exported name, e.g. "react:useState" or "express-serve-static-core:Response.json", with an @types package named after the package it is for. Python uses the dotted module path, e.g. "app.orders.Orders.find". Go uses the package import path, then the dotted name, e.g. "example.com/app/orders.Orders.Find". Rust uses the module path, e.g. "orders::Orders::find" in the crate being scanned. Only Java names include parameter types, as the other languages have no overloading.

languageVersion.description: The version of the language, e.g. "21" for Java. For SQL, the version of the database the migrations are written for, e.g. "17" for PostgreSQL 17, or "unknown" when the scanner cannot tell.

dialect.description: For SQL, the database the migrations are written for, from the driver or the Flyway or Liquibase configuration of the project, or from the SQL itself. Absent for other languages, and when the scanner cannot tell.

configuration.description: The configuration properties of the module that its code refers to or that name what it connects to, from the files its framework reads, such as application.properties and application.yml in Spring Boot, with those of each profile. Scanners record the keys the code refers to: in ${...} placeholders of annotation and call arguments, such as @KafkaListener(topics = "${orders.topic}") or @Value("${orders.topic}"); the keys under the prefix of a class bound to configuration, such as @ConfigurationProperties("app.kafka"); and the keys the values of those refer to in turn. And they record the keys a framework reads that name a destination or a path, such as the destinations of Spring Cloud Stream bindings, spring.kafka.template.default-topic or server.servlet.context-path, as each scanner lists them. Never secrets, whatever refers to them: left out are properties whose key names a secret, that is, contains password, passwd, secret, token, credential, apikey, accesskey, privatekey or authorization, in any case and ignoring "-", "_" and ".", and values that hold one: a url with a password, as in jdbc:postgresql://app:secret@db/orders, a value with password=, or a private key. Environment variables and files outside the module are not read. Absent when the scanner reads no configuration.

sourceSet.description: Whether the file is production code or test code, e.g. from src/main/java or src/test/java in Maven. Absent when the scanner cannot tell.

lineCount.description: The number of lines in the file. A file starts on line 1 and ends on line lineCount.

package.description: The qualified name of the package the file declares or belongs to, as in Package.qualifiedName. Absent for the Java default package and for languages without packages.

classes.description: The top-level classes, interfaces, enums, structs, traits and type aliases declared in the file. Nested ones are listed under the class that encloses them.

functions.description: The functions declared at the top level of the file, outside any class, with kind FUNCTION. In TypeScript and JavaScript this includes arrow functions and function expressions assigned to a top-level const, let or var, named after the variable, e.g. "src/orders:find" for "export const find = () => ..."; they are not listed again in variables. A Vue single-file component, a file with language VUE whose scripts are listed as its declarations, is its function "default", e.g. "src/components/OrderList:default": what its template uses belongs to it, at its places in the .vue file, and a template that uses it, as <OrderList :orders="orders" />, calls it with its props as named arguments. Go methods with a receiver and Rust methods in impl blocks are listed under the class of their receiver or self type instead.

variables.description: The variables and constants declared at the top level of the file, outside any class.

calls.description: The methods and constructors called by code at the top level of the file, outside any function or class, one entry per call site: module-level statements such as app.use(...) or router.get(...) in TypeScript and JavaScript, and the initializers of top-level variables. Calls inside functions and classes belong to those.

fieldAccesses.description: The fields and top-level variables read or written by code at the top level of the file, outside any function or class, one entry per access.

typeUses.description: The types referred to by code at the top level of the file, outside any function or class, other than through its calls and field accesses, one entry per use. Types of top-level variables are in their type.

migration.description: For a migration, as Flyway names its files, where it falls among the others: the server applies the migrations of a target in this order to know the tables they leave. Absent for a SQL file that is not a migration.

statements.description: For a SQL file, its statements, in the order they are written, one entry each, also for those the scanner could not read. Absent for files of other languages.

Package.description: A package of the module: a Java, Python or Go package, or a Rust module. TypeScript and JavaScript have none. Its classes are listed under the files that declare them, which name it in File.package.

name.description: The simple name. An anonymous class has none and uses the part of its binary name after the last $, e.g. "1" for "com.example.Outer$1".

qualifiedName.description: The canonical name, e.g. "com.example.Outer.Inner" for a member class. Local and anonymous classes have no canonical name and use their binary name, e.g. "com.example.Outer$1".

startLine.description: The line the declaration, including its annotations and body, starts on, starting at 1.

endLine.description: The line the declaration, including its annotations and body, ends on, inclusive.

startColumn.description: The column on startLine it starts at, starting at 1.

endColumn.description: The column on endLine it ends at, inclusive.

kind.description: CLASS, INTERFACE, ENUM, RECORD and ANNOTATION as in Java; STRUCT for Go and Rust structs; TRAIT for Rust traits; TYPE_ALIAS for a named type that is none of these, such as a TypeScript type alias, a Go defined type like "type Celsius float64" or a Rust type alias, with the type it names in aliasedType. TypeScript and Python classes are CLASS, Python protocols are INTERFACE.

nesting.description: Whether it is declared at the top level of its file, as a member of another class, inside a method body, or as an anonymous class. Absent means TOP_LEVEL.

enclosingMethod.description: For local and anonymous classes, the qualified name of the method whose body declares it.

modifiers.description: The modifiers as declared in the source.

typeParameters.description: The declared type parameters with their bounds, e.g. "T extends java.lang.Comparable<T>".

superClasses.description: The classes it extends, in declaration order. Java and TypeScript classes have at most one, Python classes can have several.

interfaces.description: The interfaces it implements, or for an interface those it extends. For Rust, the traits it implements or, for a trait, its supertraits. For Go, the interfaces an interface embeds.

aliasedType.description: For a TYPE_ALIAS, the type it names.

enumConstants.description: The constants of an enum, in declaration order.

recordComponents.description: The components of a record, in declaration order.

methods.description: Its methods and constructors. What initializers use belongs to the methods that run them: the instance initializers, field initializers and initializer blocks, to each constructor that runs them, and a class without a declared constructor lists the one the compiler adds when they use anything; the static initializers, static field initializers and static blocks, to a method named "static" with the STATIC modifier, e.g. "com.example.Orders.static()" or "src/orders:Orders.static", listed when they use anything. What the template of an Angular component uses, inline or in the file its templateUrl names, belongs to a method named "template", e.g. "src/app/orders.component:OrdersComponent.template": its bindings, events and interpolations, its pipes as calls of their transform, and the components and directives its elements use as calls of their constructors. The positions of what a template in a file of its own uses are in that file, which is listed as a file with language HTML.

fields.description: Its fields, or for TypeScript its properties. A Go embedded field is a field named after its type.

classes.description: The classes nested in this class: member classes, and local and anonymous classes declared in its methods.

startLine.description: The line the declaration, including its annotations and body, starts on, starting at 1.

endLine.description: The line the declaration, including its annotations and body, ends on, inclusive.

startColumn.description: The column on startLine it starts at, starting at 1.

endColumn.description: The column on endLine it ends at, inclusive.

kind.description: METHOD for a method, CONSTRUCTOR for a constructor (Python __init__, TypeScript constructor), FUNCTION for a function declared outside any class. A constructor has no return type.

modifiers.description: The modifiers as declared in the source.

typeParameters.description: The declared type parameters with their bounds, e.g. "T extends java.lang.Comparable<T>".

returnType.description: The declared return type. Absent for constructors, and when the source declares none and the scanner cannot infer one.

throws.description: The exception types in its throws clause.

defaultValue.description: For an element of an annotation type, its default value, with the same encoding as Annotation.arguments.

calls.description: The methods and constructors called from the body, one entry per call site. Calls inside lambdas and anonymous classes declared in the body belong to this method. A constructor also has those of the instance initializers it runs; see Class.methods.

fieldAccesses.description: The fields read or written by the body, one entry per access.

typeUses.description: The types the body refers to other than through its calls and field accesses, such as local variables, casts and instanceof checks, one entry per use.

type.description: The declared type. Absent when the source declares none and the scanner cannot infer one, as is common in Python and JavaScript.

qualifiedName.description: The qualified name of the method followed by the name of the parameter, e.g. "com.example.Orders.find(java.lang.String).id".

startLine.description: The line the declaration starts on, starting at 1.

endLine.description: The line the declaration ends on, inclusive.

startColumn.description: The column on startLine it starts at, starting at 1.

endColumn.description: The column on endLine it ends at, inclusive.

type.description: The declared type. Absent when the source declares none and the scanner cannot infer one, as is common in Python and JavaScript.

constant.description: The value of a constant, as the scanner computes it from the source: of a field or variable that cannot be assigned again and whose initializer is a constant expression, of literals and other constants. Examples are "orders.created" for static final String CREATED = "orders." + EVENT in Java with static final String EVENT = "created", and for export const CREATED = `orders.${EVENT}` in TypeScript with const EVENT = "created". A string is its text, without quotes or escapes; a number, character or boolean is its text, e.g. "3" or "true". Absent when the value is not known from the source, such as one read from the environment or returned by a call; when it is a string of more than 1000 characters; and when the name of the field or variable names a secret, as Module.configuration describes, such as API_KEY or dbPassword. Scanners never record secrets.

startLine.description: The line the declaration, including its annotations and initializer, starts on, starting at 1.

endLine.description: The line the declaration, including its annotations and initializer, ends on, inclusive.

startColumn.description: The column on startLine it starts at, starting at 1.

endColumn.description: The column on endLine it ends at, inclusive.

modifiers.description: The modifiers as declared in the source.

TypeRef.description: A type as declared, with the classes it refers to.

name.description: The type with qualified names and its type arguments, e.g. "java.util.Map<java.lang.String, com.example.Order>[]".

references.description: The qualified names of every class the type refers to, including through type arguments, bounds and array element types, e.g. ["java.util.Map", "java.lang.String", "com.example.Order"]. Primitive types and type variables are left out.

target.description: The qualified name of the method or constructor called, as in Method.qualifiedName, e.g. "com.example.OrderRepository.findById(java.lang.String)".

module.description: For a call of what a package exports, the module it is imported from as written, such as "@acme/theme" or "@acme/theme/format"; the target is then that module and the export, e.g. "@acme/theme:Button", and the call is not resolved, as the package is not scanned. Absent for a call of the scan's own code, and of anything not imported from a package.

kind.description: METHOD for a method call, CONSTRUCTOR for new, this(...) and super(...), METHOD_REFERENCE for a method or constructor reference such as Order::getId.

arguments.description: What the call passes, in the order written, one entry per argument: for a component rendered with JSX, its attributes, each under its name, without its children. Empty for a call that passes nothing, such as find(), and for a METHOD_REFERENCE, which passes nothing itself. A scanner that does not record arguments leaves them out of every call.

startLine.description: The line the call expression, including its arguments, starts on, starting at 1.

endLine.description: The line the call expression, including its arguments, ends on, inclusive.

startColumn.description: The column on startLine it starts at, starting at 1.

endColumn.description: The column on endLine it ends at, inclusive.

resolved.description: Whether the scanner resolved the target. When false, the target is the name as written in the source, e.g. because the library declaring it is not on the classpath; or, with module, because it is of a package.

Argument.description: One argument of a call, as written at the call site. It is the source, not a value: what an expression evaluates to is not known to a scanner.

name.description: The name the argument is passed under, when it is passed by name: the attribute of a JSX element, e.g. "customerId" for <OrderList customerId={id} />, or the name of a named argument in a language that has them. Absent for an argument passed by position, as in Java, and in TypeScript and JavaScript outside JSX.

value.description: The expression passed, as written in the source, with each run of whitespace, line breaks included, as one space: e.g. "id", "\"/api/orders\"" with its quotes, or "`/api/orders/${id}`" with its backticks. At most 200 characters: a longer one, such as a function passed as a callback, is cut off after 199 and ends in "…". For a JSX attribute it is the expression between its braces, e.g. "id" for customerId={id}, the string with its quotes for title="Orders", and "true" for an attribute without a value, as disabled in <Button disabled />. For a spread argument it is the expression spread, without the dots.

constant.description: The value of the argument when it is a constant expression the scanner can compute, as in Field.constant: for a literal, a constant such as Topics.CREATED, or an expression of them such as "/api" + Paths.ORDERS, e.g. "orders.created" or "/api/orders". It is computed from the whole expression, also when value is cut off. Absent for any other argument, and for a constant that names a secret.

spread.description: Whether the argument is spread, as ...ids in a call or {...props} in a JSX element. What it passes is then not known from the source: any number of arguments, or attributes of any name.

target.description: The qualified name of the field or top-level variable, as in Field.qualifiedName, e.g. "com.example.Order.id" or "src/config:settings".

access.description: READ, WRITE, or READ_WRITE for compound assignments and increments such as count++.

startLine.description: The line the field access starts on, starting at 1.

endLine.description: The line the field access ends on, inclusive.

startColumn.description: The column on startLine it starts at, starting at 1.

endColumn.description: The column on endLine it ends at, inclusive.

resolved.description: Whether the scanner resolved the target. When false, the target is the name as written in the source, e.g. because the library declaring it is not on the classpath.

target.description: The qualified name of the class used.

kind.description: How the body uses the type. Types in the signature are in returnType and the parameters, and instantiations are CONSTRUCTOR calls.

startLine.description: The line the type starts on, starting at 1.

endLine.description: The line the type ends on, inclusive.

startColumn.description: The column on startLine it starts at, starting at 1.

endColumn.description: The column on endLine it ends at, inclusive.

resolved.description: Whether the scanner resolved the target. When false, the target is the name as written in the source, e.g. because the library declaring it is not on the classpath.

Modifier.description: A modifier as declared, or the visibility a language gives through other means. Go reports PUBLIC for exported names. Rust reports PUBLIC for pub and INTERNAL for pub(crate). DEFAULT is a Java default method; EXPORT and EXPORT_DEFAULT are TypeScript and JavaScript export and export default. Python reports STATIC and ABSTRACT for @staticmethod and @abstractmethod, and the decorators as annotations.

startLine.description: The line the annotation, including its arguments, starts on, starting at 1.

endLine.description: The line the annotation, including its arguments, ends on, inclusive.

startColumn.description: The column on startLine it starts at, starting at 1.

endColumn.description: The column on endLine it ends at, inclusive.

arguments.description: The arguments, by name, as JSON values: literals as strings, numbers and booleans; arrays as lists; class literals as the qualified type with .class, e.g. "java.lang.String.class"; nested annotations as annotations. A constant whose value the scanner knows, such as Topics.CREATED, or an expression of them, such as "/api" + Paths.ORDERS, is its value, as in Field.constant, e.g. "/api/orders". Other references, such as enum constants, are their qualified name, e.g. "org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestMethod.GET", and anything else is its source. The argument of a single-member annotation, such as @Path("/orders"), is named "value", as in Java; the arguments of a TypeScript decorator are encoded the same way.

Annotation.description: A Java annotation, a TypeScript or Python decorator, or a Rust attribute such as #[derive(Debug)].

name.description: The name the build system knows it by: "group:artifact" for Maven and Gradle, the package name for npm and Python, e.g. "@scope/package" or "requests", the module path for Go, e.g. "github.com/google/uuid", and the crate name for Cargo.

transitive.description: Whether it is pulled in through another dependency rather than declared by the module.

module.description: The path of the module in this scan result it refers to, when it is another module of the same target rather than an external library.

ConfigurationProperty.description: A configuration property, as written in a configuration file.

key.description: The key, with the keys of nested maps joined by dots and the items of lists as [index], as written, e.g. "spring.kafka.template.default-topic" or "app.topics[0]".

value.description: The value as written, without quotes: a number or boolean as its text, e.g. "3" or "true", and placeholders as they are, e.g. "${ORDERS_TOPIC:orders.created}", as the code that reads it resolves them.

file.description: The path of the file, relative to the target, e.g. "src/main/resources/application-prod.yml".

profile.description: The profile the property is for, from the name of its file, e.g. "prod" for application-prod.yml, or from the document of a YAML file it is in, e.g. spring.config.activate.on-profile: prod. Absent for the default configuration.

line.description: The line of the file the property is on, starting at 1.

name.description: The imported name as written, without a trailing wildcard, e.g. "java.util.List", "java.util" for java.util.*, or "java.util.Collections.emptyList" for a static import.

static.description: Whether it is a static import.

wildcard.description: Whether it imports every member, as in java.util.*.

startLine.description: The line the import statement starts on, starting at 1.

endLine.description: The line the import statement ends on, inclusive.

startColumn.description: The column on startLine it starts at, starting at 1.

endColumn.description: The column on endLine it ends at, inclusive.

qualifiedName.description: The qualified name of the enum followed by the constant, e.g. "com.example.Status.OPEN".

startLine.description: The line the constant, including its arguments and body, starts on, starting at 1.

endLine.description: The line the constant, including its arguments and body, ends on, inclusive.

startColumn.description: The column on startLine it starts at, starting at 1.

endColumn.description: The column on endLine it ends at, inclusive.

startLine.description: The line the component starts on, starting at 1.

endLine.description: The line the component ends on, inclusive.

startColumn.description: The column on startLine it starts at, starting at 1.

endColumn.description: The column on endLine it ends at, inclusive.

Migration.description: Where a migration falls among those of its target, from the name of its file, e.g. V13__notification_recipients.sql in Flyway.

kind.description: VERSIONED: applied once, in the order of the versions, e.g. V13__name.sql. REPEATABLE: applied again whenever it changes, after the versioned ones, e.g. R__views.sql. UNDO: undoes the versioned migration of its version, e.g. U13__name.sql.

version.description: The version, as written in the name of the file, e.g. "13" or "2.1"; compared part by part as numbers, so "2.10" comes after "2.9". Absent for a repeatable migration.

description.description: The description from the name of the file, with underscores as spaces, e.g. "notification recipients".

ColumnDefinition.description: A column as a statement defines it.

name.description: The name of the column, unquoted and as written, e.g. "user_id".

type.description: The type as written, in lower case, e.g. "uuid", "varchar(255)" or "timestamp with time zone".

nullable.description: Whether the column takes null: false with NOT NULL or as part of the primary key. Absent when the statement does not say, as for ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE.

primaryKey.description: Whether the column is, or is part of, the primary key of its table.

unique.description: Whether the column is unique on its own.

default.description: The default as written, e.g. "now()" or "false".

table.description: The table referenced, as in Statement.table.

column.description: The column referenced; absent when the statement leaves it to the primary key of the table.

onDelete.description: What deleting the referenced row does to the referencing ones; absent for NO ACTION.

ColumnChange.description: What an ALTER TABLE statement changes of a column.

kind.description: ADD and DROP add and remove the column; RENAME renames it to newName; ALTER_TYPE changes its type to that of definition; SET_NOT_NULL, DROP_NOT_NULL, SET_DEFAULT and DROP_DEFAULT change what it takes; ADD_FOREIGN_KEY and DROP_FOREIGN_KEY change what it references, as definition.foreignKey says.

column.description: The column changed, by its name before the statement.

newName.description: For RENAME, the new name of the column.

definition.description: For ADD, the column added; for ALTER_TYPE, SET_DEFAULT and ADD_FOREIGN_KEY, what of it changes.

Statement.description: A SQL statement, as written in a file: what it does to the tables of the database, not the state they end up in, which the server works out from the migrations in order.

kind.description: What the statement does. OTHER for one that changes no table or view, such as INSERT, GRANT or CREATE FUNCTION, and for one the scanner could not read.

table.description: The table or view the statement creates, changes or drops, or the table of an index, unquoted, with its schema when written so, e.g. "notification_recipients" or "billing.invoices".

newName.description: For RENAME_TABLE, the new name of the table.

columns.description: For CREATE_TABLE, its columns, in order; for CREATE_INDEX, the columns indexed.

changes.description: For ALTER_TABLE, what it changes of the columns, in order.

references.description: The other tables the statement depends on: those a view reads, and those its foreign keys reference.

ifExists.description: Whether it is written IF EXISTS or IF NOT EXISTS, so applies only to a table or view that exists, or does not.

parsed.description: Whether the scanner read the statement. False for one it could not, such as of a dialect it does not know: kept with its lines and kind OTHER, so a report can say what it did not understand.

startLine.description: The line the statement starts on, starting at 1.

endLine.description: The line the statement ends on, with its semicolon.
